name: Rhodesia (1964–1968)
description: A light-blue ensign — a sky-blue field with the Union Flag in the canton — charged in the fly with the shield of the Rhodesian arms: a green field with a gold pick above a red chief bearing a white lion between two thistles.
history: Southern Rhodesia replaced its blue ensign with this light-blue ('RAF blue') version on 8 April 1964 to distinguish itself from the other British colonial ensigns; it was flown from 22 April and confirmed on 26 May 1964. It remained the flag through the Unilateral Declaration of Independence of 11 November 1965 and was replaced on the third anniversary of UDI, 11 November 1968, by the green-white-green flag.

features.role: shield from the Rhodesian coat of arms: gold pick, red chief with white lion and thistles
features.symbolism: mining, and the Rhodes family arms
